content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: overtime for 8 general agents 13:00-15:00, plus delayed general breaks and IVR callback, for ₹2,880. Predicted service level is 85.5% for 12:00-15:30 against an 80% target.","why":"General is short because of a sick wave, not extra demand. There are 9 unplanned absences against a usual 2.4, and only 9 agents were on the phones at 08:00 against 15 planned. Calls (23 vs 23.5 forecast) and handle time (384s vs 375s) are close to plan. With no action, service level is predicted to fall to 75.5% over 12:00-15:30, with general at 72.7%. P2 adds cover directly on general and lifts both queues: general to 84.9% and payments to 86.0%. Abandons drop from 5.2% to 3.5%, and rest of day is predicted at 91.6%. It breaks no policies.","trade_offs":["P1 costs nothing but only reaches 79.4%, just under target. Its general queue sits right at 80.0% with no margin, and abandons are 4.7%.","P3 costs the same ₹2,880 but does worse overall: 84.3%, abandons 3.7%, rest of day 90.8%. It moves cross-skilled agents off payments, which drops payments to 82.9%, while general gets slightly more (86.2% vs 84.9%).","P2 leaves payments staff in place. That matters because payments also has high absence today (6 against a usual 2.6)."],"watch":"Check that enough of the 8 general agents actually accept the overtime; if uptake is low, the 85.5% forecast won't hold. Keep watching payments absence. The diagnosis rests on only one interval of data, so re-check service level after the next interval or two."}
